summary: Round 2 re-verification. Checked 27 claims, found 0 critical mirages. All three Round 1 critical findings RESOLVED in the updated tech-spec: (1) tests/test_llm_common.py reference dropped — spec lines 29 + 233 now correctly route the list_item patching test through the existing tests/test_openrouter_transcreation.py which already exercises _patch_text_with_ru_paragraphs; (2) preview_nodes vs _build_content_from_blocks confusion fixed — spec lines 14, 18, 28, 53, 163 now consistently identify _build_content_from_blocks as the actual rendering loop and preview_nodes as the dispatcher (matches telegraph_publisher.py:114 and :253 respectively); (3) <li> handler self-contradiction resolved — spec lines 14 + 38 now consistently say 'inline in _walk reusing _runs_from_tag, no separate helper function'. One minor accuracy note (non-blocking).

findings.claim: tech-spec line 233: 'All existing tests in tests/test_openrouter_transcreation.py and tests/test_claude_transcreation.py (_patch_text_with_ru_paragraphs for paragraph/heading/lead — list_item flows through naturally because we extend the _PATCHED_TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES tuple, no new test file is needed).'
findings.reality: Only tests/test_openrouter_transcreation.py imports and exercises _patch_text_with_ru_paragraphs directly (line 317: test_patch_text_with_ru_paragraphs_splices_in_order; line 331: openrouter_transcreation._patch_text_with_ru_paragraphs(...)). tests/test_claude_transcreation.py does NOT call _patch_text_with_ru_paragraphs by name — it tests the Claude-specific transcreation flow. The spirit of the claim is correct (both engines share _llm_common._PATCHED_TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES, so extending the tuple changes both code paths uniformly), but the line-233 claim is over-stated: only the OpenRouter test file actually exercises the patcher.
findings.fix: Optional: tighten to '...test_openrouter_transcreation.py exercises _patch_text_with_ru_paragraphs directly; test_claude_transcreation.py covers the Claude path which shares the same _PATCHED_TEXT_BLOCK_TYPES via _llm_common — no new test file needed.' Non-blocking, no critical/major impact.
